notable_absence.finding: This page tabulates 40 distinct HTTP method/URI pairs across four REST APIs and carries not a single version annotation - no "available since", no "new in 8.0", no "deprecated", no per-endpoint version column. For a wave whose priority is version-gating vocabulary this is the most significant thing on the page: the Query REST API index is entirely version-blind, so a reader cannot tell from it whether /admin/gc, /evaluator/v1/libraries or /settings/querySettings/curlWhitelist exist in 7.x. The four API tables would be the natural place for an availableSince column and it is absent. Note that version information for these endpoints DOES exist downstream - server/current/n1ql-rest-query/index.md contains e.g. "In clusters running Couchbase Server 6.5 and later, this parameter is ignored and has no effect" for encoded_plan - so the absence is an index-page gap, not an absence of the underlying facts. requiresPrivilege is likewise wholly absent from this page; see cross_component_finding.

cross_component_finding:
Three things this index page states about the API family that the twelve pages in this directory do not individually state, plus the error model the eleven example pages establish collectively (recorded here once, per the batch instruction, rather than repeated in eleven records):

(1) SETTINGS TIER SPLIT ACROSS SERVICES. The three-tier settings hierarchy (cluster / node / request) is split across two different services' ports: node-level Query settings are POSTed to /admin/settings on the Query Service's own ports 8093/18093, while cluster-level Query settings are POSTed to /settings/querySettings on the Cluster Manager's ports 8091/18091. So configuring the Query Service requires talking to the Cluster Manager. The registry's existing dependsOnService predicate captures the service dependency but not this "configured through a different service's API" shape; if reconciliation wants that shape, configuredViaService would be the predicate.

(2) THE ADMIN API MIRRORS THE SYSTEM KEYSPACES. /admin/prepareds, /admin/active_requests and /admin/completed_requests expose exactly the resources already modelled as system keyspaces in earlier rounds (n1ql:system-prepareds, n1ql:system-active-requests, n1ql:system-completed-requests, n1ql:system-vitals via /admin/vitals). Two access surfaces - SQL++ SELECT against system: and HTTP GET against /admin/ - over one resource set. I have deliberately NOT asserted an identity relation, because this page never says the two are the same thing; it is offered as a reconciliation question. A predicate along the lines of alsoExposedAs / hasAlternativeAccessSurface would be needed, and note the registry already has incompatibleWithAccessSurface, i.e. it has vocabulary for surfaces being incompatible but none for surfaces being equivalent.

(3) THE ERROR MODEL OF THE QUERY REST API (from exsuccessful/exrequesterror/exserviceerror/exn1qlerror/extimeout/exunsupportedhttp). All responses share one envelope: requestID, optional signature, optional results, optional errors[], status, metrics. The error taxonomy is three-way and the three kinds are distinguished by *where* the fault is, not by shape: a request error is "a problem with the REST request itself, e.g. missing a required parameter" (code 1050, status fatal, HTTP 200); a SQL++ error is "an error processing the SQL++ statement in a request" (codes 3000, 12003, status fatal, HTTP 200); a service error is "a problem that prevents the request being fulfilled" ("Request queue full", status errors, HTTP 503). Request errors and SQL++ errors are therefore indistinguishable by status - both are fatal - and both arrive with HTTP 200; only the service error changes the HTTP status. Timeout is a fourth, separate status value and is the only case carrying a per-error "retry": true flag and the only case that returns results (an empty array) alongside errors. The single exception to the envelope is the unsupported HTTP method, which returns a bare "HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed" with no JSON body at all - method rejection happens before a requestID is allocated, so there is nothing to correlate that failure to in system:completed_requests. That asymmetry is the most operationally consequential fact in the set and it is stated nowhere in prose.

(4) AUTHENTICATION PRECEDENCE IS DOCUMENTED ELSEWHERE, NOT HERE. exauthhttp.md and exauthrequest.md demonstrate the two credential mechanisms but neither states which wins when both are present. server/current/n1ql-rest-query/index.md does: "If a request contains both HTTP basic authentication header and a `creds` parameter, the `creds` parameter is ignored and only the HTTP basic authentication header is used for authenticating." The precedence rule is thus only reachable from the reference page, not from either example page nor from this index.
cross_product_finding:
THE HEADLINE FINDING FOR THIS BATCH: the entire server/current/n1ql/n1ql-rest-api/ directory has no Capella counterpart. There is no cloud/n1ql/n1ql-rest-api/ directory and no linked-data/poc/extractions/cloud/n1ql/n1ql-rest-api/ records; cloud/n1ql/ contains only query.md, n1ql-intro/, n1ql-language-reference/ and n1ql-manage/. All twelve pages in this batch are Server-only, and the absence is structural rather than accidental.

What Capella offers instead, and why it is not the same concept:

- cloud/n1ql/query.md enumerates Capella's query surfaces as "the Query tab in the Couchbase Capella UI, the cbq shell, the Data API, or the Couchbase SDKs" - four surfaces, none of them a directly-addressed Query Service REST API. The registry's capella:query-tab, capella:cbsh, capella:data-api and capella:management-api are the Capella-side ids; n1ql:query-service-rest-api minted here is a fifth, Server-only concept and must not be merged with any of them.

- Capella DOES reach the same underlying endpoint, but only through the Data API proxy path. cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md and cloud/data-api-guide/data-api-use.md both use "$BASEURL/_p/query/query/service" - the /_p/query/ prefix is a Cluster Manager passthrough, and $BASEURL is a hostname, never a port. Server's examples in this batch all use "http://localhost:8093/query/service" directly. So the relationship is: same wire protocol and same request/response envelope, reached via a proxied path on Capella and via a dedicated service port on Server. This is what the minted port:* concepts and usesPort predicate are for - the Server records can state port exposure and the Capella records structurally cannot, which makes the divergence machine-visible instead of merely narrated. It also means data-api:passthrough-endpoint (already coined in the Capella rounds) is the Capella-side counterpart of n1ql:query-service-rest-api, and reconciliation should link them with a cross-product predicate rather than by identity.

- The administrative half of this batch has no Capella analogue at any level. Capella documents no /admin/* endpoints, no /admin/settings node-level configuration, and no /settings/querySettings; cluster and node configuration is an operation of the Capella control plane (capella:management-api, capella:cluster-manager), not of a Query Service port. This is the clean statement of the Server/Capella split for the Query Service: the *data plane* is shared (proxied on Capella), the *management plane* is entirely disjoint. That matches the pattern the earlier Capella rounds recorded from the other direction.

- Consequently the RBAC/credential divergence the brief warns about does not even arise on these pages - not because the two models agree, but because Capella has no page here to state a credential requirement on. The Server side states its requirement (Administrative or Query & Index RBAC roles) only on the downstream n1ql-rest-query reference page, not in this directory.
version_finding:
1. No version or edition gating anywhere on this page or in this directory - see notable_absence. Not one of the twelve pages in this batch contains the strings "and later", "since", "deprecated", "removed in", "Enterprise Edition" or "Community Edition". So this batch contributes no availableSince / deprecatedIn / requiresEdition instances at all, and that negative result is itself the batch's version finding: the Query REST API documentation is version-unannotated end to end, in contrast to the SQL++ language reference pages (which the earlier rounds show are densely annotated) and in contrast to the n1ql-rest-query parameter reference (which carries per-parameter version notes such as encoded_plan's 6.5 note).

2. IMPLICIT VERSIONING IN A URI. /evaluator/v1/libraries is the only versioned path in the whole 40-endpoint surface: the Query Functions REST API embeds "v1" in its path while the Query Service, Query Admin and Query Settings APIs are unversioned. This is an in-band API version marker with no prose explaining it, and no statement of what v0 or v2 would mean. Worth flagging because it is the one place the Query REST API expresses a version at all, and it does so in a form no availableSince relation would capture.

3. A RENAME VISIBLE ONLY AS AN INCONSISTENCY. The URI segment is curlWhitelist but the documented feature name is "CURL Access List", in both the GET and POST rows: "| GET | /settings/querySettings/curlWhitelist | [Retrieve CURL Access List](../../n1ql-rest-settings/index.md#get%5Faccess) |". The whitelist-to-access-list rename has clearly landed in the prose and the anchor (#get_access, #post_access) but not in the wire path, which is presumably frozen for compatibility. I have NOT recorded this as a renamedFrom relation, because the page does not state a rename - it merely exhibits one. Reconciliation may want it, and if so the shape needed is not renamedFrom (which relates two names of one thing across versions) but something like retainsLegacyWireName, distinguishing a documented name from a frozen identifier. This is a real gap: the registry currently cannot express "renamed in the docs but not in the API".

4. Documentation defect, minor: the See Also section links to "[Configure Queries](../n1ql-manage/query-settings.md)" using a single ../, while every table link in the same page uses ../../ to reach sibling modules (../../n1ql-rest-query/, ../../n1ql-rest-admin/). Both are correct - n1ql-manage is inside the n1ql module and n1ql-rest-query is a separate module at server/current/n1ql-rest-query/ - but the inconsistency is worth noting since it is the kind of thing that looks like a broken xref and is not one. All ten table link targets were verified to exist.
